reviews.text:
My pet is a patient here.

I think it's a great animal hospital with a kind and caring veterinarian and friendly staff who provide thorough examinations.

Once, my cat seemed unwell on a day the hospital was closed, so I called outside of business hours, but it went to voicemail. I had to take her to another hospital urgently. It turned out to be just a mild case of gastroenteritis, but I remember feeling so relieved when the veterinarian called back after we got home and she had calmed down, asking, "Is she okay?"

I've used several animal hospitals, including those recommended by pet shops and others in emergencies, but Bear Animal Hospital seems to be the best fit for us.

I asked the staff who were cleaning for directions and they were very kind and helpful! I realized it was outside of business hours, sorry! Thanks to the staff, I arrived safely♪ Thank you so much, it's reassuring to leave my pet with such kind staff!

For about two years, I took my beloved cat to this veterinary clinic for kidney problems.

Although my cat has passed away, the doctor and reception staff were incredibly kind and helpful throughout my visits.

I am truly saddened by my cat's passing, but she fought bravely until the very end. And above all, I am so glad that we were able to take her to Bear Animal Hospital. ☺️

When the doctor and reception staff examined my cat, they would say things like,
"You're doing great!" and "We hope you keep fighting!"

Those words comforted me so many times.

There are various reviews, but I think the doctor is a bit shy! 😂

He explains things carefully to answer my questions and has a great sense of humor. 🥹

The time I spent talking with the doctor and reception staff was a source of comfort during my visits. Thank you so much.

Also, I learned that the doctor regularly attends study groups or academic conferences, and I was very happy to know that he is a dedicated veterinarian.

I have another cat, so I will likely be using their services again in the future.


Thank you so much for everything over the past two years.

My dog ​​has been a puppy here for over 10 years.

The vet is kind and excellent.

We've been taking care of our cat here.

I think this hospital is perfect for owners who take good care of their pets and can administer medication as instructed by the doctor.

The examinations and treatments are appropriate, and there's no unnecessary treatment or sales pressure, making it trustworthy.

Our cat was on the verge of kidney failure, but thanks to this hospital, she's now healthy.

Regarding other health issues, following the instructions for medication and receiving IV fluids at the hospital has prevented them from worsening and has led to improvement.

We've never felt any unfriendliness or poor service; it's a very courteous hospital.

Thank you always.
I took my one-year-old cat for a vaccination. The vet was very friendly.

We recently had surgery performed on one of our Djungarian hamster's eyes at this veterinary clinic.

They answered all our questions thoroughly, and while they offer careful and leisurely service, this is a veterinary clinic I would recommend to anyone with an urgent injury or needing immediate attention.

Our hamster's eye was protruding, requiring emergency treatment, so I'm glad we entrusted him to Bear's Clinic.

Even though we could only pick him up after 3 PM due to our schedule, outside of business hours, they welcomed us in and thoroughly explained his condition.

They reassured us that he was doing well after the surgery, and I'm truly glad we came here.

If anything comes up again, I will definitely entrust him to them.

Thank you so much for everything.

The nurse was very kind, but the doctor's attitude was terrible. I was told that my pet needed emergency surgery, but he only gave vague answers about the details and procedures of the surgery, which is something the hospital should explain. About five minutes after I walked in, he said, "It's surgery. What do you want to do?" in a bad mood, and as a layperson, I didn't know what to do. I asked various questions like, "Is it going to be admitted today?" but he only said, "Yes. Today. Surgery tomorrow." I was worried about entrusting my pet to such a rude doctor, so I immediately went to a different hospital and had the surgery done there. During the examination, he kept saying things like, "This one will die soon," and just kept making me anxious without giving any detailed explanations, which was just unpleasant. There were good reviews as well, so I didn't believe the bad reviews that much, but now I understand why. This is the first time I've ever felt so uncomfortable at an animal hospital.

I've been taking care of my dog ​​here. The doctor answers all my questions, and the nurses are kind and reassuring. There aren't many places that treat small animals, and when my first rabbit 🐇 got sick, they taught me about oxygen chambers and other necessary things, and they were there to see her off at the end. They tell you what's necessary, they give clear diagnoses, they do everything you ask, and there's no pushy sales pitch, so I think they're very conscientious.

There are mixed reviews, but I feel completely at ease entrusting my pet to this hospital. Since they moved, the waiting areas for dogs and cats are separate, which is much more comfortable!

I'll continue to rely on them in the future.

I had my female cat spayed here, but I felt very untrustworthy.

First of all, the wound after the surgery was very rough, completely different from the wounds on cats I had spayed at other hospitals later, which made me very uneasy.

Furthermore, the doctor explained that there was no need to remove the stitches, but when I went to another hospital just to be sure, I was told that the stitches would need to be removed. These inconsistent explanations made me distrustful.

Also, I was told that spaying and neutering stray cats would be cheaper, but in reality, I was told that it was only cheaper if a resident doctor performed the surgery. I was unsure about leaving my precious cat in the care of a resident doctor, so I ended up asking a regular doctor, but this kind of behavior does not make this a hospital I can trust.

I think you really need to be careful when using this hospital, in order to protect your precious family members.

I don't even want to give it one star! I rescued a kitten and it was a little past the opening hours, so I wondered if they'd take a look? I peeked through the door, but they just shooed me away without even asking me why! I should have read the reviews before going. Apparently they've changed their name several times... They're not vets or anything, they're just after the money. The worst!

The amount of medicine was probably too small for my dog, so we visited the hospital once and gave him the medicine until it ran out, but he had bloody stools again, so we were given the same medicine again on our second visit.
The medicine was also a very small amount, and now that we've finished it, the symptoms have returned,
I'm starting to feel suspicious that they want us to keep coming back to the hospital.
To make matters worse, the bill for the second visit was expensive, even though it was just a follow-up visit.
The diarrhea has completely cleared up with the medicine we got from another nearby hospital.
I probably won't go there again.

I went to the doctor with cat fungus. They prescribed a topical ointment, and when I went back about two weeks later, they said, "It's cured," so I was relieved. Then, something strange happened again, so I went back for a follow-up visit. They said, "It's recurred, please apply the ointment again," so I applied the ointment again. This went on for a year. The last time I went, it recurred again ⇒ ointment ⇒ complete cure ⇒ a few days later, they removed the cat fungus. I went to another hospital, but instead of being cured, the cat fungus had spread all over my body, so I had to put my whole body under general anesthesia and shave my head. Furthermore, because I continued to apply the ointment I was given as instructed, I ended up developing another skin condition. If you don't know anything about skin, wouldn't it be better to just say, "I don't know. Please go to another hospital"? Try to put yourself in the shoes of a cat who is put under general anesthesia and has their entire body shaved. How would you feel if you were suddenly put under general anesthesia and woke up to find your entire body shaved? It's better to be honest and say you don't know, rather than making a random diagnosis. I love cats, so I'll never forget this, not even in my next life.

My dog ​​suddenly lost his appetite and wasn't feeling well, so I took him to the vet. He had giardiasis, but he had always eaten despite it, so I was worried and brought him here. I explained that he wouldn't eat but would eat strange things like wallpaper. I was finally called in for an examination, but it was over in 3 minutes. It was way too quick, and I asked about his appetite, but they just said it was giardiasis and a stomach ache, prescribed some medicine, and that was it. The next day, his condition worsened, so I went to a different hospital where they said he had liver problems and had to hospitalize him. If you're a veterinarian, you should examine your dog properly. I will never go back here again. I'm writing this review to prevent other people from becoming victims. Honestly, I don't even want to give it one star.

I had my cat examined here, and all I was told was that kidney stones were found. I was sent home without any information about treatment. After researching at home, I found that medication and surgery were necessary, and despite paying nearly 30,000 yen, the examination was over in about 5 minutes. When I got home, I noticed a wound on my cat's head, and since my cat is not the type to struggle when touched by anyone, I am extremely suspicious. The fact that many other reviews are 1 star is proof that there is always smoke without fire. I get the feeling from their attitude that this hospital is only in business for the money and has no compassion or emotion whatsoever.

I'm a regular patient here with my cat. During a check-up, she was diagnosed with early-stage kidney failure, but she's now in remission from stage 3 to normal levels.

The doctor and nurses are incredibly kind and caring, and I feel completely at ease leaving my cat in their care. I also appreciate that the waiting areas are separated for cats and dogs.

I recently got a pet and used their services for the first time, and it was a terrible experience. I had called beforehand to inquire about the services and fees for the initial consultation. The person on the phone was friendly and explained things clearly, so I took my pet in, but the actual experience was completely different. After putting my pet on a simple scale, they only did a few seconds of palpation. The doctor remained silent throughout, saying nothing, and then suddenly said it was over. When I asked if they could do the detailed check-up and apply preventative medication that I had been told about on the phone, they curtly replied, "It's not necessary."

In conclusion, it was just a three-minute perfunctory examination (if you can even call it that), with no advice or words of encouragement. I paid several thousand yen for the initial consultation, but I feel like I wasted my money and time without knowing what I went there for. I would never entrust my beloved pet to this clinic if it were ever ill. I'm glad I found out about it early.

This is the worst hospital I've ever been to; I wouldn't even give it one star.

My dog ​​has suffered permanent damage as a result.

My dog ​​accidentally ingested a clump of its own fur and was in distress, so I took it to this hospital. They gave it an injection to induce vomiting, but no fur came out. They prescribed medication and told me to monitor it, so I went home. Two hours later, my dog ​​had a seizure, foamed at the mouth, and its eyes rolled back. I immediately called the hospital, and they asked me to bring it in, but they said the seizure had stopped and that it was fine now. They didn't do anything, just that.

To top it all off, they said the injection they gave earlier had the potential to cause seizures... This was the result of giving the injection without any explanation beforehand.

After returning home, the same symptoms continued every few hours. I took my dog ​​to the emergency hospital. They provided thorough treatment and a proper explanation, and the doctor at the emergency hospital explained that the symptoms might continue until the medication from the injection wore off, and that there was a possibility of permanent damage.

About half a month has passed since that day, but even now that the medication has worn off, there are still days when he has seizures.
Why did I choose that hospital?
I regret it so much.
That veterinarian had no knowledge, no love, and no skill.
I really wish that hospital would go out of business.
My cat had blood in its urine, so I took it to the vet. It was 7:50 PM, past the last appointment time, but they saw it outside of regular hours, and the nurse was very kind. …

I took my cat to the vet because she was walking strangely. They only took an X-ray and sent me home saying there was nothing wrong, but I wasn't satisfied, so I took her to another hospital. They did blood tests and it was discovered that …

I visited this vet because my dog ​​had a cough, but they just told me to give him medicine and sent me home without explaining what the illness was. I continued giving him the medicine for two weeks, but it had no effect. When I went to …

The clinic is very clean.
More than anything, the doctors are very kind and I trust them.
The nurses are also very nice.
If I need anything, I can call Bear right away.

There are mixed reviews about this hospital, but personally, I think it's a trustworthy animal hospital.
The waiting rooms are separated for dogs and cats and are clean and tidy.
They are very kind and attentive to well-behaved pets.
This was my first time using their services, and they listened to me very kindly and carefully. …
